rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both establish a new national monument under section 2 of the 1906 act and use the same operative sequence: reservation subject to valid existing rights, a detailed boundary description, an almost verbatim warning, and National Park Service administration under the 1916 act. C20 and C23 are also strong comparators, especially as Kennedy-era monument proclamations, but C01 has the closest combined operative wording and provision sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do proclaim that, subject to valid existing rights, there is hereby reserved and set apart, as the Buck Island Reef National Monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do proclaim that, subject to valid existing rights, there is hereby reserved and set apart as a national monument, to be known as the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively close language establishes and names a new monument through the same reservation formula.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WARNING is expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved for the monument by this proclamation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Warning is hereby given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved by this proclamation.
shared_material.explanation: The warning provisions are nearly verbatim and occupy the same position after the land description.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of the Interior shall have the supervision, management, and control of this monument as provided in the act of Congress entitled "An act to establish a National Park Service, and for other purposes," approved August 25, 1916
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Monument shall be supervised, managed, and controlled in accordance with the act of Congress entitled "An Act To Establish a National Park Service and for Other Purposes," approved August 25, 1916
shared_material.explanation: Both assign monument administration through materially the same National Park Service statutory machinery immediately after the warning.
